title: Applications of sequence and series in daily life
competency: Solve real-life problems with arithmetic and geometric sequences and series.

keywords.def: A sequence where each term is the previous term plus a fixed number.
The fixed number r: r = next term ÷ this term.
A sum a₁ + a₂ + a₃ + … that never ends.

en.text: A fixed raise, a fixed extra amount each day, or a pattern that grows by the same number is arithmetic. Use Aₙ for one value (the 10th salary) and Sₙ for a total (pay over 12 months). If n is unknown, Sₙ = total gives a quadratic; keep only the positive whole-number root.

am.text: ቋሚ የደሞዝ ጭማሪ ወይም በየቀኑ ቋሚ ተጨማሪ አሪትሜቲክ ነው። ለአንድ እሴት Aₙ፣ ለድምር Sₙ እንጠቀማለን።

screens.title: A rising salary
screens.ask: A salary starts at 5200 ETB a month and rises 320 ETB every month. What is it in month 10?
screens.after:
Month 1 has no raise. Month 2 has 1 raise, so month 10 has 9 raises.
A₁₀ = 5200 + 9 × 320 = 5200 + 2880 = 8080 ETB.
(8400 ETB counts 10 raises: the most common slip.)

screens.title: Applications of sequences and series
paras: Many real problems are arithmetic or geometric sequences.
Ask: is the same amount added each time? Then it is arithmetic.
One value → use Aₙ.  A total → use Sₙ.

screens.title: A salary that rises each month
screens.ask: Move the start, the raise and the month. Compare one month with the total.
outs: Total so far: Sₙ = n(A₁ + Aₙ)/2
screens.note: 5200 ETB with +320 for 12 months: 8720 ETB in month 12, 83 520 ETB in all.

screens.title: Key word
defs: A sequence where each term is the previous term plus a fixed number.

screens.ask: Arithmetic series in real life: same salary (5200 ETB, +320 each month). Total earned in the first year = ___ ETB
screens.why:
Step 1: a total means a sum: use Sₙ with n = 12 months.
Step 2: last term A₁₂ = 5200 + 11 × 320 = 5200 + 3520 = 8720.
Step 3: S₁₂ = 12(5200 + 8720)/2 = 6 × 13 920.
Step 4: = 83 520 ETB.
(8720 is one month's pay, not the total.)
screens.clue: A year is 12 months. Find A₁₂, then S₁₂.

screens.title: 192 window frames: 5 on day 1, 2 more each day
steps: Days cannot be negative: n = 12 days.

screens.title: One term or a total?
screens.text: Sort each question: does it need one term Aₙ or a sum Sₙ?
items: Money earned in the first year
screens.why:
"In month 10" or "the 18th prize" asks for one value: use Aₙ = A₁ + (n − 1)d.
"Earned in the first year" or "made in 12 days" adds every term: use Sₙ.
This is the first decision in every word problem.
screens.clue: Does the question add up many terms, or ask for one?

screens.ask: Solve for n in a word problem: a theatre fills by 4, 6, 8, … people each minute. After 6 minutes it is half full. It is full after ___ minutes
screens.why:
Step 1: A₁ = 4, d = 2. S₆ = (6/2)[8 + 5 × 2] = 3 × 18 = 54.
Step 2: half full is 54, so it holds 108.
Step 3: Sₙ = (n/2)[8 + 2(n − 1)] = n(n + 3) = 108.
Step 4: n² + 3n − 108 = 0, (n + 12)(n − 9) = 0, so n = 9 (time cannot be negative).
(Trap: 12 minutes doubles the time, but the rate keeps rising.)

screens.ask: Arithmetic series in real life: a salary of Birr 32 500 a year rises Birr 1 400 a year. Total over the first 10 years = Birr ___
screens.clue: 10 times the average of the first and last salary.

screens.ask: One value from an arithmetic sequence: Bontu saves Birr 1 000 in year 1 and Birr 200 more each year. In year 8 she saves Birr ___
screens.why:
Step 1: one year's amount means one term: A₈.
Step 2: year 8 has 7 increases: A₈ = 1 000 + 7 × 200.
Step 3: = 1 000 + 1 400 = Birr 2 400.

screens.ask: Arithmetic series in real life: 18 prizes, the first is Birr 10 000 and each is Birr 500 less. Total value = Birr ___
Solve for n in a word problem: letters in columns, A has 1, B has 3, C has 5, … The pattern has 361 letters in all. The last column's letter is the ___ th letter of the alphabet
screens.why:
Step 1: 1, 3, 5, … is arithmetic: A₁ = 1, d = 2.
Step 2: Sₙ = (n/2)[2 + 2(n − 1)] = (n/2)(2n) = n².
Step 3: n² = 361, so n = 19.
The 19th letter is S.
screens.clue: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n².

en.text: When a quantity changes by the same percentage each period, multiply by (1 + rate) for growth or (1 − rate) for loss. After n periods: amount × (1 ± rate)ⁿ. Interest, population growth, depreciation and radioactive decay all work this way.

am.text: አንድ መጠን በየጊዜው በአንድ መቶኛ ሲለወጥ ለዕድገት በ (1 + ምጣኔ) ለቅናሽ በ (1 − ምጣኔ) እናባዛለን። ከ n ጊዜ በኋላ፡ መጠን × (1 ± ምጣኔ)ⁿ።

screens.title: Interest on a deposit
screens.ask: Birr 3 500 earns 6% interest a year. How much is in the account after 1 year?
screens.after:
Interest: 6% of 3 500 = 0.06 × 3 500 = 210.
Amount: 3 500 + 210 = 3 710 = 3 500 × 1.06.
Each year multiplies by 1.06, so the amounts are geometric.
(3 560 adds only 60; 3 506 adds 6.)

screens.title: Why the amounts are geometric
steps: The ratio of neighbours is always 1.06.
So the amounts form a geometric sequence.

screens.title: Grow or shrink by a percentage
screens.ask: Set the start amount, the yearly rate (negative for a loss) and the years.
screens.note: −10% for 4 years from Birr 28 000 gives Birr 18 370.80.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The fixed number r: r = next term ÷ this term.

screens.text: Geometric growth and decay: an item loses one tenth of its value each year. What is the common ratio?
screens.why:
Step 1: it loses 1/10 each year.
Step 2: it keeps 1 − 1/10 = 9/10 of its value.
Step 3: next value = 0.9 × this value, so r = 0.9.
(0.1 is the part lost, not the ratio.)
screens.clue: What fraction of the value is kept?

screens.title: Match each change to its ratio r
screens.text: Match each yearly change to its common ratio r.
screens.why:
Growth of p%: r = 1 + p/100, so 6% → 1.06 and 2.5% → 1.025.
Loss of p%: r = 1 − p/100, so 12% → 0.88.
Losing 1/10 keeps 9/10 → 0.9. Halving keeps 1/2 → 0.5.
screens.clue: r is the part that is KEPT: 1 plus the growth, or 1 minus the loss.

screens.ask: Geometric decay: 100 g of a substance loses half its mass each year. After 10 years ___ g is left
screens.why:
Step 1: r = 1/2, start 100 g.
Step 2: after 10 years: 100 × (1/2)¹⁰.
Step 3: 2¹⁰ = 1 024, so 100/1 024 ≈ 0.098 g.
(Trap: 100 − 10 × 50 treats halving as subtraction.)

screens.ask: Geometric decay: an item worth Birr 28 000 loses 1/10 each year. After 4 years it is worth Birr ___
screens.why:
Step 1: r = 0.9 (it keeps 9/10).
Step 2: after 4 years: 28 000 × 0.9⁴.
Step 3: 0.9² = 0.81, and 0.81 × 0.81 = 0.6561.
Step 4: 28 000 × 0.6561 = Birr 18 370.80.
(28 000 − 4 × 2 800 = 16 800 takes 1/10 of the first value each year: wrong.)

screens.ask: Geometric growth: a town of 100 000 grows 2.5% a year. In 10 years it has about ___ people
screens.why:
Step 1: r = 1 + 0.025 = 1.025.
Step 2: after 10 years: 100 000 × 1.025¹⁰.
Step 3: 1.025¹⁰ ≈ 1.28008.
Step 4: ≈ 128 008 people. (Adding 2 500 a year gives 125 000: growth on growth is missing.)

screens.text: Compound interest: Sofia deposits Birr 3 500 at 6%. Which gives the amount at the end of year n?
screens.why:
Step 1: end of year 1: 3500(1.06).
Step 2: end of year 2: 3500(1.06)².
Step 3: each year adds one more factor 1.06.
So after n years: 3500(1.06)ⁿ. (The power n − 1 is for Gₙ when G₁ is the deposit itself.)

screens.ask: Geometric decay: a boat worth Birr 34 000 loses 12% a year. After 5 years it is worth about Birr ___
screens.why:
Step 1: it keeps 100% − 12% = 88%, so r = 0.88.
Step 2: after 5 years: 34 000 × 0.88⁵.
Step 3: 0.88⁵ ≈ 0.52773.
Step 4: 34 000 × 0.52773 ≈ Birr 17 942.89.
(Trap: r = 0.12 keeps only 12% each year.)

ideas.name: Totals that never pass a limit

en.text: If each new amount is a fixed fraction of the last, the total is an infinite geometric series. Its sum G₁/(1 − r) is the limit the total approaches but never passes, like a flower whose growth halves each year or nested squares whose areas halve.

am.text: እያንዳንዱ አዲስ መጠን የቀደመው ቋሚ ክፍልፋይ ከሆነ ድምሩ ኢውሱን ጂኦሜትሪክ ተከታታይ ነው። G₁/(1 − r) ድምሩ የማያልፈው ወሰን ነው።

screens.title: A flower that slows down
screens.ask: A 110 cm flower grows 10 cm in year 1, then half as much each year. Can it reach 140 cm?
screens.after:
Growth: 10 + 5 + 2.5 + 1.25 + … cm: a geometric series with r = 1/2.
Total growth S∞ = 10/(1 − 1/2) = 20 cm.
So the height stays below 110 + 20 = 130 cm. It never reaches 140 cm.

screens.title: The flower's growth, 20 cm at most
screens.ask: The bar is 20 cm. Tap ▶ to add each year's growth.
screens.after: 18.75 cm after 4 years. Each year fills half of the gap, so the 20 cm bar is never quite full.

screens.title: A limit for the total
paras: Every partial sum is less than 20, so the height never passes 130 cm.

screens.title: Key word
defs: A sum a₁ + a₂ + a₃ + … that never ends.

screens.text: Sum to infinity in geometry: nested squares, each square's area is half the one before. The first area is a². The total area is
screens.why:
Step 1: the areas are a², a²/2, a²/4, …
Step 2: G₁ = a², r = 1/2.
Step 3: S∞ = a²/(1 − 1/2) = a²/(1/2) = 2a².
(a² is only the first square.)

screens.title: A bouncing ball
steps: Drop from h. Each bounce reaches r × the last height.

screens.ask: Sum to infinity for a bouncing ball: dropped from 10 m, it rebounds to 50% of its height each time. Total distance = ___ m
screens.why:
Step 1: down 10 m, then up and down 5 m, 2.5 m, …
Step 2: total = h(1 + r)/(1 − r) with h = 10, r = 0.5.
Step 3: 10 × 1.5/0.5 = 15/0.5 = 30 m.
Check: 10 + 2(5 + 2.5 + …) = 10 + 2 × 10 = 30 ✓. (20 m forgets that each bounce goes up and down.)

screens.ask: Sum to infinity in geometry: equilateral triangles, each side is the height of the one before. The first has side 2. The total area is ___ (as a decimal, 2 places)
screens.why:
Step 1: the height of a side-s triangle is (√3/2)s, so the sides shrink by r = √3/2.
Step 2: areas shrink by the square: (√3/2)² = 3/4.
Step 3: first area = (√3/4) × 2² = √3.
Step 4: total = √3/(1 − 3/4) = 4√3 ≈ 6.93.
(Trap: using r = √3/2 for the areas.)

screens.text: A limit for the total: true or false? Growth of 6 cm, then 3 cm, then 1.5 cm, … can add up to more than 12 cm.
screens.why:
Step 1: G₁ = 6, r = 1/2.
Step 2: S∞ = 6/(1 − 1/2) = 12.
Step 3: every partial sum is less than 12 (6, 9, 10.5, …).
So it can never pass 12 cm: false.

screens.ask: Sum to infinity for a bouncing ball: dropped from 8 m, it rebounds to 3/4 of its height each time. Total distance = ___ m

items.ask: One value from an arithmetic sequence: salary in month 10 (5200 ETB, +320 a month) = ___ ETB
items.why:
Step 1: month 10 has 9 raises.
Step 2: A₁₀ = 5200 + 9 × 320 = 5200 + 2880.
Step 3: = 8080 ETB.

items.ask: Arithmetic series in real life: total salary in the first year (5200 ETB, +320 a month) = ___ ETB
Solve for n in a word problem: 192 frames, 5 on day 1, +2 each day. Number of days = ___
items.why:
Step 1: A₁ = 5, d = 2: Sₙ = (n/2)[10 + 2(n − 1)] = n(n + 4).
Step 2: n(n + 4) = 192, so n² + 4n − 192 = 0.
Step 3: (n + 16)(n − 12) = 0.
Step 4: days are positive: n = 12.

items.ask: One value from an arithmetic sequence: starting salary Birr 25 250 a year, raise Birr 250 every 6 months. Salary at the end of year 3 = Birr ___
items.why:
Step 1: 2 raises a year for 3 years = 6 raises.
Step 2: 6 × 250 = 1 500.
Step 3: 25 250 + 1 500 = Birr 26 750.
(See the teacher note: the book's wording is ambiguous.)

items.ask: One value from an arithmetic sequence: Bontu saves Birr 1 000 in year 1, +200 each year. Year 8 = Birr ___
items.why:
Step 1: year 8 has 7 increases.
Step 2: 1 000 + 7 × 200 = 1 000 + 1 400.
Step 3: = Birr 2 400.

items.ask: Geometric decay: Birr 28 000, losing 1/10 a year. After 4 years: Birr ___
Geometric decay: a boat worth Birr 34 000 loses 12% a year. After 5 years: about Birr ___
Geometric growth: a town of 100 000 grows 2.5% a year. In 10 years: about ___ people
Compound interest: Birr 3 500 at 6%. Amount at the end of year 2 = Birr ___
items.why:
Step 1: r = 1.06; two years means two factors.
Step 2: 1.06² = 1.1236.
Step 3: 3 500 × 1.1236 = Birr 3 932.60.

items.ask: One value from an arithmetic sequence: Firm A pays Birr 31 100, +1 200 a year. Year 11 salary = Birr ___
items.why:
Step 1: year 11 has 10 raises.
Step 2: 10 × 1 200 = 12 000.
Step 3: 31 100 + 12 000 = Birr 43 100.

items.ask: Arithmetic series in real life: Firm B pays Birr 35 100, +900 a year. Total over 11 years = Birr ___

items.text: Compare two arithmetic series: over 11 years, which firm pays more, and by how much?
items.why:
Step 1: Firm A: A₁₁ = 43 100, S₁₁ = 11(31 100 + 43 100)/2 = 408 100.
Step 2: Firm B: S₁₁ = 435 600.
Step 3: 435 600 − 408 100 = 27 500.
So B pays Birr 27 500 more, even though A's raise is bigger.

items.ask: Work backwards from the sum: 10 prizes total Birr 13 250, each Birr 250 less than the one before. The first prize = Birr ___

items.text: Sum to infinity for a bouncing ball: a ball dropped from h rebounds to a fraction r of its height. Total distance:
items.why:
Step 1: down h, then each bounce goes up and down: 2rh, 2r²h, …
Step 2: rh + r²h + … = rh/(1 − r).
Step 3: total = h + 2rh/(1 − r) = h(1 − r + 2r)/(1 − r).
Step 4: = h(1 + r)/(1 − r). (h/(1 − r) counts each bounce only once.)
items.clue: Each bounce goes up and down.

items.text: Sum to infinity in geometry: equilateral triangles, each side = the height of the one before; the first side is a. Total area:
items.why:
Step 1: first area G₁ = (√3/4)a².
Step 2: sides shrink by √3/2, so areas shrink by r = 3/4.
Step 3: S∞ = (√3/4)a² ÷ (1/4) = (√3/4)a² × 4.
Step 4: = √3 a².

notes.text: Exercise 1.22 Q1 is ambiguous: counting the raise at the 3-year mark gives Birr 26 750 (used here); not counting it gives Birr 26 500.
Example 6 b compares total (cumulative) expenses and income and gets n ≈ 30.3; if it means yearly expenses vs yearly grant, expenses are higher from year 16. Example 6 is not used in graded items.
Example 4 uses G₁ = the deposit, so Gₙ is the amount after n − 1 years; Exercise 1.23 Q4 e asks for the amount after n years, 3500(1.06)ⁿ. Lessons say this explicitly.
Exercise 1.25 Q1 says "r %" but the formula needs r as a fraction (60% → 0.6).
Exercise 1.24 Q3 assumes the first prize is the largest (d = −250).
The book uses Figure 1.5 twice (tree, p.35; letter pattern, p.45).

screens.text: Sum an arithmetic sequence with Sₙ = n(A₁ + Aₙ)/2: A₁ = 2, A₈ = 23. S₈ = ?
screens.why:
Step 1: n = 8, first 2, last 23.
Step 2: S₈ = 8(2 + 23)/2 = 4 × 25.
Step 3: = 100.
(200 forgets to halve.)

math.geometric-nth-term.name: The nth term of a geometric sequence

screens.text: Find a term with Gₙ = G₁ rⁿ⁻¹: G₁ = 100, r = 0.5. G₃ = ?
Sum to infinity, S∞ = G₁/(1 − r): 20 + 10 + 5 + … = ?
